Plots for the formulation change described in `docs/problem-formulation.md`.
All runs: random initialization (all four angles 0.5), COBYLA, reps 2, at most 1000 iterations, trial 1, same code.
Only `qubo-formulation` differs.

| Workload | Old formulation (q2o) | New formulation (qaoa) | Best plan cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1: 3 relations, 2 predicates | Week99 (5 qubits) | Week96 (3 qubits) | 15 |
| P2: 4 relations, 2 predicates | Week100 (12 qubits) | Week97 (8 qubits) | 315 |
| P3: 4 relations, 6 predicates | Week101 (20 qubits) | Week98 (8 qubits) | 29 (29.4, stored as an integer) |

The two formulations put energies on different scales. Compare energies between them with the
normalized plots (1 = starting energy, 0 = lowest possible energy), not the raw values.

```{r}
# Paths and per-run constants. Chunks run with the working directory set to graphs/.
root <- normalizePath("..")
sub_dir <- "ExperimentalAnalysis/IBMQ/QPUPerformance/Results/CPU_Data/iterations_1000/reps_2/COBYLA"

runs <- tribble(
  ~problem, ~formulation, ~week, ~input_idx, ~ground_energy, ~target,
  "P1", "q2o",  99,  0, 1.0310081, 15,
  "P1", "qaoa", 96,  0, 1.1760913, 15,
  "P2", "q2o",  100, 1, 4.7663813, 315,
  "P2", "qaoa", 97,  1, 3.6532125, 315,
  "P3", "q2o",  101, 2, 2.7249943, 29,
  "P3", "qaoa", 98,  2, 2.3344538, 29
)

energy_csv <- function(week, input_idx) {
  glue("{root}/outputs/uninitialized/energy/Week{week}/{sub_dir}/input{input_idx}/trial1/energy_per_iteration_1000_COBYLA_2_1.csv")
}
final_readout <- function(week) {
  glue("{root}/outputs/uninitialized/Week{week}/{sub_dir}/trial_1/readout_summary.csv")
}
first_readout <- function(week, input_idx) {
  glue("{root}/outputs/uninitialized/Week{week}/{sub_dir}/input{input_idx}/trial1/readout_summary_eval1.csv")
}
run_of <- function(p, f) runs %>% filter(problem == p, formulation == f)
```

```{r}
# Energy vs cost boxplot of one readout; returns the share of samples at `target` (from qcdkm.rmd)
cost_energy_boxplot_prob <- function(file_path, show_points = TRUE,targetCol="cost",thresh="()",opt="",fallback=FALSE,target,label="") {
  library(readr)
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(ggplot2)

  lines <- readLines(file_path, warn = FALSE)
  start_idx <- grep("^#\\s*all_solutions\\s*$", lines)

  if (length(start_idx) == 0) {
    stop("no # all_solution find")
  }

  all_lines <- lines[(start_idx + 1):length(lines)]
  all_lines <- all_lines[all_lines != ""]

  df <- read_csv(
    I(paste(all_lines, collapse = "\n")),
    show_col_types = FALSE
  )

  if (!("probability" %in% names(df)) && ("prob" %in% names(df))) {
    df <- df %>% rename(probability = prob)
  }

  df <- df %>%
    transmute(
      used_fallback=as.logical(used_fallback),
      cost = as.numeric(.data[[targetCol]]),
      energy = as.numeric(energy),
      probability = as.numeric(probability)
    ) %>%
    filter(is.finite(energy), probability > 0,used_fallback == fallback)

  w0 <- min(df$probability)
  df_exp <- df %>%
    mutate(w = pmax(1L, round(probability / w0))) %>%
    uncount(w)

  p <- ggplot(df_exp, aes(x = factor(cost), y = energy)) +
    geom_boxplot() +
    theme_bw() +
    labs(x = targetCol, y = "Energy",
         title = glue("{label}Energy vs {targetCol}; opt:{opt}; used_fallback={fallback}"))

  if (show_points) {
    # qcdkm.rmd used one legend break per distinct probability; with hundreds of bitstrings
    # (P2, P3) that legend covers the plot, so ggplot picks a few breaks instead
    p <- p +
      geom_point(
        data = df,
        aes(size = probability),
        alpha = 0.5,
        position = position_jitter(width = 0.15, height = 0)
      ) +
      scale_size_continuous(name = "probability")
  }
  cost_counts <- df %>%
  count(cost, name = "n_rows") %>%
  mutate(pct = n_rows / sum(n_rows)) %>%
  arrange(cost)
  print(glue("Matrix for used_fallback={fallback}"))
  print(cost_counts)
  print(p)

return(list(
  cost_counts[cost_counts$cost == target, ]$pct
))  }
```

```{r}
# Energy over iterations of one run (from visualization.rmd)
plot_energy_from_csv <- function(file_path, baseline = NULL) {
  df <- read.csv(file_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  energy <- df$energy

  y_limits <- if (!is.null(baseline)) {
    range(c(energy, baseline), na.rm = TRUE)
  } else {
    range(energy, na.rm = TRUE)
  }

  if ("iteration" %in% colnames(df)) {
    plot(
      df$iteration, energy,
      type = "b",
      pch = 19,
      xlab = "Iteration",
      ylab = "Energy",
      main = "Energy over Iteration",
      ylim = y_limits
    )
  } else {
    plot(
      seq_along(energy), energy,
      type = "b",
      pch = 19,
      xlab = "Index",
      ylab = "Energy",
      main = "Energy",
      ylim = y_limits
    )
  }

  if (!is.null(baseline)) {
    abline(h = baseline, col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 2)
    legend(
      "topright",
      legend = c("Energy", "Ground state energy"),
      col = c("black", "red"),
      lty = c(1, 2),
      pch = c(19, NA),
      bty = "n"
    )
  }

  return(energy)
}
```

```{r}
# Several energy-over-iteration curves on one plot, legend in its own strip below
# (layout from seeded-multi-spiq.rmd). curves: list of list(file, label, col, ground).
# normalise = TRUE plots (E - ground) / (E_start - ground): 1 = start, 0 = lowest possible energy,
# which puts formulations with different energy scales on one axis. normalise = FALSE plots raw
# energies with one dashed ground-state line per curve, in the curve's colour.
plot_energy_curves <- function(curves, normalise = FALSE, main = "Energy vs Iteration (QAOA)") {
  dfs <- lapply(curves, function(cv) {
    df <- read.csv(cv$file)
    if (normalise) df$energy <- (df$energy - cv$ground) / (df$energy[1] - cv$ground)
    df
  })
  refs <- if (normalise) 0 else sapply(curves, `[[`, "ground")

  x_range <- range(unlist(lapply(dfs, `[[`, "iteration")), na.rm = TRUE)
  y_range <- range(c(unlist(lapply(dfs, `[[`, "energy")), refs), na.rm = TRUE)
  y_pad <- 0.05 * diff(y_range)
  if (y_pad == 0) y_pad <- 1
  y_range <- c(y_range[1] - y_pad, y_range[2] + y_pad)

  old_par <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
  on.exit(par(old_par))
  layout(matrix(1:2, ncol = 1), heights = c(5, 1))
  par(mar = c(4, 4, 4, 2) + 0.1)

  plot(NA, xlim = x_range, ylim = y_range, xlab = "Iteration",
       ylab = if (normalise) "Normalized energy (1 = start, 0 = ground state)" else "Energy",
       main = main)
  for (k in seq_along(curves)) {
    lines(dfs[[k]]$iteration, dfs[[k]]$energy, col = curves[[k]]$col, lwd = 1)
    points(dfs[[k]]$iteration, dfs[[k]]$energy, col = curves[[k]]$col, pch = 16, cex = 0.3)
    if (!normalise) abline(h = curves[[k]]$ground, col = curves[[k]]$col, lwd = 1.5, lty = 2)
  }
  if (normalise) abline(h = 0, col = "green3", lwd = 1.5, lty = 2)
  grid()

  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
  plot.new()
  labels <- sapply(curves, `[[`, "label")
  cols <- sapply(curves, `[[`, "col")
  ref_labels <- if (normalise) "ground state energy" else paste(labels, "ground")
  ref_cols <- if (normalise) "green3" else cols
  legend("center", ncol = 2,
         legend = c(labels, ref_labels),
         col = c(cols, ref_cols),
         lwd = c(rep(1, length(curves)), rep(1.5, length(ref_cols))),
         lty = c(rep(1, length(curves)), rep(2, length(ref_cols))),
         pch = c(rep(16, length(curves)), rep(NA, length(ref_cols))),
         bty = "n")
}
```

```{r}
# Optimal ratios of every boxplot below, collected for the summary tables
ratio_rows <- list()
record_ratio <- function(problem, formulation, stage, fallback, res, target) {
  pct <- unlist(res)
  ratio_rows[[length(ratio_rows) + 1]] <<- data.frame(
    problem = problem, formulation = formulation, stage = stage, used_fallback = fallback,
    optimal_cost = target, optimal_ratio = if (length(pct) == 0) 0 else pct[1]
  )
}

# Final and first-iteration readouts of one run, raw and fallback decoding: 4 boxplots + 4 recorded ratios
readout_boxplots <- function(p, f) {
  r <- run_of(p, f)
  for (stage in c("final", "first iteration")) {
    path <- if (stage == "final") final_readout(r$week) else first_readout(r$week, r$input_idx)
    for (fb in c(FALSE, TRUE)) {
      print(glue("{p}, {f} (Week{r$week}), {stage}, used_fallback={fb}; optimal cost {r$target}"))
      res <- cost_energy_boxplot_prob(path, targetCol="cost", thresh=150, opt="COBYLA", fallback=fb, target=r$target,
                                      label = glue("{p} {f} (Week{r$week}), {stage}: "))
      record_ratio(p, f, stage, fb, res, r$target)
      print(glue("optimal ratio ({if (fb) 'fallback' else 'raw'}) = {round(unlist(res)[1], 4)}"))
    }
  }
}
```

## All three workloads together (new formulation)
Each workload has its own energy scale, so the curves are normalized: 1 = starting energy, 0 = lowest possible energy.
```{r}
new_curves <- lapply(c("P1", "P2", "P3"), function(p) {
  r <- run_of(p, "qaoa")
  list(file = energy_csv(r$week, r$input_idx), label = glue("{p} (Week{r$week})"),
       col = c(P1 = "blue", P2 = "red", P3 = "purple")[[p]], ground = r$ground_energy)
})
plot_energy_curves(new_curves, normalise = TRUE, main = "New formulation, random initialization: P1-P3")
```

# 3. Old vs new formulation

## Optimal ratios
Share of samples whose decoded plan has the best cost. "raw" reads the order straight from the bits; "fallback" repairs it to avoid cross joins.
```{r}
ratio_summary <- do.call(rbind, ratio_rows) %>%
  mutate(decoding = if_else(used_fallback, "fallback", "raw"),
         stage = factor(stage, levels = c("first iteration", "final")),
         formulation = factor(formulation, levels = c("q2o", "qaoa")))

ratio_summary %>%
  select(problem, stage, decoding, formulation, optimal_ratio) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = formulation, values_from = optimal_ratio) %>%
  select(problem, stage, decoding, q2o, qaoa) %>%
  arrange(problem, stage, decoding) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Optimal ratio, old (q2o) vs new (qaoa) formulation, random initialization")
```
```{r, fig.width=9, fig.height=6}
ggplot(ratio_summary, aes(x = problem, y = optimal_ratio, fill = formulation)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.75) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.3f", optimal_ratio)),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), vjust = -0.3, size = 3) +
  facet_grid(stage ~ decoding) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(q2o = "grey55", qaoa = "steelblue")) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Workload", y = "Optimal ratio", fill = "Formulation",
       title = "Optimal ratio: old vs new formulation (random initialization)")
```

## Start and final energies
"Share of the way to the bottom" = (start − best seen) / (start − lowest possible): 0 = no progress, 1 = reached the ground state.
This is the fair comparison across formulations, since their raw energies are on different scales.
```{r}
energy_summary <- runs %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    e = list(read.csv(energy_csv(week, input_idx))$energy),
    evaluations = length(e),
    start_energy = e[1],
    final_energy = e[length(e)],
    best_energy = min(e),
    share_to_bottom = (start_energy - best_energy) / (start_energy - ground_energy)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(problem, formulation, week, evaluations, ground_energy, start_energy, final_energy, best_energy, share_to_bottom)

knitr::kable(energy_summary, digits = 3, caption = "Energies, old (q2o) vs new (qaoa) formulation, random initialization")
```
```{r, fig.width=8, fig.height=4}
ggplot(energy_summary, aes(x = problem, y = share_to_bottom, fill = formulation)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.75) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", share_to_bottom)),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), vjust = -0.3, size = 3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(q2o = "grey55", qaoa = "steelblue")) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Workload", y = "Share of the way to the ground state", fill = "Formulation",
       title = "How far the optimizer got: old vs new formulation")
```

## Energy over iterations: old vs new
For each workload: the normalized plot first (fair comparison), then raw energies with each formulation's own ground-state line.
```{r}
compare_curves <- function(p) {
  lapply(c("q2o", "qaoa"), function(f) {
    r <- run_of(p, f)
    list(file = energy_csv(r$week, r$input_idx),
         label = glue("{if (f == 'q2o') 'old' else 'new'} ({f}, Week{r$week})"),
         col = if (f == "q2o") "blue" else "red", ground = r$ground_energy)
  })
}
```

### P1
```{r}
plot_energy_curves(compare_curves("P1"), normalise = TRUE, main = "P1: old vs new formulation (normalized)")
plot_energy_curves(compare_curves("P1"), normalise = FALSE, main = "P1: old vs new formulation (raw energy)")
```
